problem:
Prove that ${\sum }_{i=3}^{n}(2i+3)=(n+6)(n-2)$ using mathematical induction.

We proceed using induction on $n.$

**Base Case**: We first prove that our statement is true for the base case $n=\,${{field-1}}.

For the left-hand side, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=3}^{3}(2i+3)={{field-2}}\end{aligned}
$$

which equals the right-hand side. Thus, our statement is {{field-3}} for $n=3.$

**Inductive Hypothesis**: We assume that for some $n=$ {{field-4}}, we have

$$
{\sum }_{i=3}^{k}(2i+3)={{field-5}}.
$$

**Inductive Step**: To prove $P(k+1),$ we write

$$
{\sum }_{i=3}^{k+1}(2i+3)=({\sum }_{i=3}^{k}(2i+3))+{{field-6}}.
$$

By the inductive hypothesis, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}({\sum }_{i=3}^{k}(2i+3))+2(k+1)+3 & ={{field-7}} \\  & ={{field-8}},\end{aligned}
$$

as required.

Therefore, by the principle of induction, ${\sum }_{i=3}^{n}(2i+3)=(n+6)(n-2)$ is true for all {{field-9}}.
